overview.text: The Black-tailed Rattlesnake is a venomous rattlesnake of the south-western United States and Mexico, named for its all-black tail.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually 76 to 107 cm; the largest recorded about 125 to 130 cm. Females tend to be larger.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Arizona, New Mexico and western and central Texas, and Mexico south to Oaxaca, up to about 2,930 m.

behaviour.text: Active by day in spring and autumn, and more at night in summer.

diet.text: Rodents and other small mammals, birds and small lizards.

reproduction.text: Mates in spring and gives birth to live young.

recognise.text: Black tail ending in a rattle.
